newsitem.title: CHINA: Philippines GNP growth seen at 10-12 pct by 2002.
newsitem.headline: Philippines GNP growth seen at 10-12 pct by 2002.

text.p: The Philippines will register annual growth in gross national product (GNP) of 10 to 12 percent by 2002, Secretary of Trade and Industry, Cesar Bautista, said on Wednesday.

"Philippine development has been progressing at a very satisfactory rate since five years ago," Bautista told a news briefing held as part of the current meeting of the International Chamber of Commerce in Shanghai.
"Our target is to continue this growth so that in the year 2002, which is five years down the road, our GNP will register a growth of about 10 to 12 percent," he added.
The Philippines annual GNP grew 6.8 percent in 1996 and is forecast to exceed seven percent this year.
Economic growth has been driven by exports and the government plans to further increase the competitiveness of the country's products with the rest of the world, Bautista said.
